title: The Emperor's New Clothes
author: Hans Christian Andersen (安徒生)
summary: 酷爱新衣的虚荣皇帝迎来了两个狡诈的骗子，宣称能织出天下最华美且‘愚蠢或不称职者看不见’的神奇衣服。满朝文武与万千百姓为了掩饰自卑纷纷附和赞美，直到盛大游行大典上，一个纯真孩童喊出了真相。

paragraphs.author: Hans Christian Andersen (安徒生)
paragraphs.en:
The Emperor's New Clothes
Hans Christian Andersen (安徒生)
paragraphs.zh: 《皇帝的新装》 · Hans Christian Andersen (安徒生)

paragraphs.en: Many years ago, there was an Emperor, who was so excessively fond of new clothes, that he spent all his money in dress. He did not trouble himself in the least about his soldiers; nor did he care to go to the theatre, except to show off his new clothes. He had a different coat for every hour of the day.
paragraphs.zh: 许多年前，有一位皇帝极度痴迷于新衣服，把自己所有的钱财全挥霍在穿戴打扮上。他对自己麾下的军队漠不关心，既不屑于去看戏，也不热衷于游园巡行，唯一热衷的便是在众人面前炫耀他的华服。他一天之中的每一个小时都要换一套不同的衣袍。

paragraphs.en: Life was very merry in the great town in which he lived; strangers arrived every day. One day two swindlers came. They said that they were weavers, and declared that they could manufacture the finest cloth to be imagined. Their colours and patterns, they said, were not only exceptionally beautiful, but the clothes made of their material possessed the wonderful quality of being invisible to any man who was unfit for his office, or unpardonably stupid.
paragraphs.zh: 在他居住的那座大都城里，人们生活得十分快活，每天都有各方异国宾客来访。有一天来了两个江湖骗子，自称是手艺高超的织工，扬言能织出世人所能想象的最上乘精致的布料。他们吹嘘这布料不仅花色图案绝美无双，更拥有一种神奇非凡的特性：凡是不称职的官员，或者愚蠢透顶无药可救的人，全都会对这种布料视而不见。

paragraphs.en: 'Those must be splendid clothes,' thought the Emperor. 'By wearing them I could easily find out what men in my kingdom are unfit for their places; and I would be able to tell the wise from the foolish. Yes, that cloth must be woven for me immediately!' And he gave large sums of money to the swindlers that they might begin their work at once.
paragraphs.zh: “那定是世间少有的华服宝衣！”皇帝暗自思忖，“穿上它们，我便能轻而易举揪出帝国里滥竽充数的昏官；我也能将聪明智者与愚蠢之徒甄别得一清二楚！是的，必须立刻为我开机纺织这种神布！”于是他当即赏赐给两个骗子一大笔巨款，命他们即刻开工。

paragraphs.en: They set up two looms, and made show of working, though they had nothing at all on the looms. They at once requested the finest silk and the purest gold thread, which they put into their knapsacks, and worked on the empty looms until late at night.
paragraphs.zh: 两个骗子立刻架设起两台织布机，装模作样地忙活起来，尽管织机上空空如也，连一根丝线都没有。他们当即索要了最顶级的绫罗绸缎与最纯粹的赤足金线，随手塞进自己的行囊腰包，然后坐在空荡荡的织机前热火朝天地假装忙碌到深夜。

paragraphs.en: 'I should like to know how they are getting on with the cloth,' thought the Emperor. But he felt a little uneasy when he remembered that he who was not fit for his office could not see it. So he sent his faithful old Minister to the weavers. 'He will be best able to see how the cloth looks,' thought the Emperor, 'for he is a man of sense, and no one can be more suitable for his office than he.'
paragraphs.zh: “我很想知道这布料织得究竟如何了，”皇帝心想。但一想到不称职之人无法看见布料，他心头也不免有些忐忑不安。于是，他决定派遣那位德高望重的老大臣先去织房查探。“他定能洞悉布料究竟织得何等华美，”皇帝盘算道，“因为他为人明智干练，论称职绝无任何人能胜过他。”

paragraphs.en: Now the good old Minister went into the room where the swindlers sat before the empty looms. 'Heaven preserve us!' thought the old Minister, opening his eyes very wide. 'I cannot see anything at all!' But he did not say so. The swindlers invited him to step nearer, and asked if he did not admire the exquisite pattern and the beautiful colours.
paragraphs.zh: 这位可敬的老大臣走进了织房，只见两个骗子正煞有介事地端坐在空织机前忙碌。“上帝保佑啊！”老大臣瞪大了双眼暗自惊呼，“我怎么什么东西也看不见啊！”但他绝不敢将这句话吐露出口。骗子们殷勤地邀请他走近细瞧，询问他是否赞叹这绝美的纹理与惊艳的花色。

paragraphs.en: Poor old Minister! He looked and looked, but he could not see anything, because there was nothing there. 'Am I a fool?' thought he. 'I must never let anyone know it. Can it be that I am unfit for my office? No, that must not be said either.' 'I shall say nothing about my not seeing the cloth,' thought the old man. 'Oh, it is very pretty! It has quite charmed me!' he declared aloud.
paragraphs.zh: 可怜的老大臣！他伸长了脖子看了又看，却依旧什么也瞧不见，因为织机上本来就空无一物。“难道我真是个大蠢才？”老大臣吓得冷汗直流，“我绝不能让任何人看出这一点！难道我当真不配坐稳大臣之位？不，这种话更不能走漏半点风声！”“噢，太漂亮了！这花色真是令我叹为观止！”老大臣连忙大声由衷赞叹道。

paragraphs.en: The Emperor soon sent another worthy courtier to see how the weaving was progressing. It was the same with him as with the first; he looked and looked, but as there was nothing upon the empty looms, he could see nothing. 'Is it not a beautiful piece of cloth?' asked the two swindlers, explaining the magnificent pattern which did not exist at all.
paragraphs.zh: 不久之后，皇帝又派遣了另一位体面的近臣前去视察织布进展。他的遭遇与老大臣如出一辙：他眯起双眼看了又看，可面对空空如也的织机，他什么也没能看到。“大人，这布料难道不够美轮美奂吗？”两个骗子指手画脚地向他大肆夸耀着那根本不存在的神奇花纹。

paragraphs.en: 'I am not stupid,' thought the man. 'It must be that I am not fit for my good, profitable office! That is very strange; I must take care that nobody notices it.' So he praised the cloth he did not see, and assured the weavers of his delight in the lovely colours. 'Yes, it is magnificent!' he said to the Emperor.
paragraphs.zh: “我可绝不是个愚民笨蛋，”这位近臣暗忖，“那肯定是由于我不称职，不配享受这份肥缺美差了！这真叫人匪夷所思，不过我得千方百计别让同僚察觉！”于是他也极尽词藻赞美那团空气，向皇帝信誓旦旦地汇报：“回禀陛下，那布料当真乃天上人间绝无仅有的绝世神品！”

paragraphs.en: The whole town was talking of the splendid cloth. At last the Emperor wished to see it himself, while it was still upon the loom. Accompanied by a select number of officers, including the two honest officials who had already been there, he went to the crafty impostors, who were working with might and main, though without any thread on the looms.
paragraphs.zh: 整座城里的臣民都在奔走相告谈论着这匹天衣神布。终于，皇帝按捺不住，决定在布料尚未下机前亲自前去先睹为快。在一众显赫大臣与前两位老臣的簇拥下，皇帝驾临工坊，只见那两个狡黠的骗子正汗流浃背地手脚并用忙活个不停，尽管机上依旧连半根游丝都没有。

paragraphs.en: 'Is not the work magnificent?' said the two officials. 'Does not your Majesty admire the pattern and the colours?' and they pointed to the empty looms. 'How is this?' thought the Emperor. 'I can see nothing at all! This is terrible! Am I a fool? Am I not fit to be Emperor? That would be the most dreadful thing that could happen to me.'
paragraphs.zh: “陛下，这手艺难道不宏伟壮丽吗？”前两位大臣谄媚地指向空织布机，“难道陛下不赞赏这图案与色泽吗？”“这是怎么回事？”皇帝心里咯噔一下，暗自惶恐，“我竟然什么也瞧不见！这太可怕了！难道我是个白痴？难道我不配做这帝国的皇帝？这可是天下最致命的灭顶之灾啊！”

paragraphs.en: 'Oh, it is very pretty!' said the Emperor aloud. 'It has our highest approbation!' and he nodded pleasantly, and examined the empty looms with great satisfaction; for he would not say that he could not see what the two officials had praised so much.
paragraphs.zh: “噢，太美了！”皇帝立刻满脸堆笑大声宣布，“朕赐予它最高的赞赏与嘉许！”他煞有介事地满意点头，饶有兴致地仔细端详着空空的机轴；因为他无论如何也绝不能承认，自己竟然看不见两位大臣交口称赞的无上宝物。

paragraphs.en: The Emperor appointed the two swindlers 'Imperial Court Weavers,' and ordered that they should make a suit of clothes of the splendid cloth for the great procession that was to take place. The swindlers sat up all night, and burnt more than sixteen candles, that people might see how busy they were to get the Emperor's new clothes ready.
paragraphs.zh: 皇帝当即敕封两个骗子为“御用织造大师”，并严令他们连夜用这匹神奇面料赶制出一整套绝世礼服，以便皇帝在即将举行的盛大巡游大典上御驾穿戴。两个骗子通宵达旦彻夜未眠，点亮了十六根大蜡烛，好让所有人都能亲眼见证他们赶制天衣有多么辛劳忙碌。

paragraphs.en: At last the swindlers announced: 'The Emperor's new clothes are ready!' The Emperor came himself with his grandest courtiers, and the swindlers held up their arms, as if they were holding something. 'These are the trousers! this is the coat! here is the mantle!' and so on. 'It is as light as a spider's web; one would almost imagine one had nothing on, but that is the high quality of the delicate fabric.'
paragraphs.zh: 终于，骗子们高声宣告：“皇帝陛下的新衣已告落成！”皇帝率领满朝重臣亲自驾临试衣。两个骗子高高举起双手，仿佛端着沉甸甸的无价之宝：“瞧，这是长裤！这是上衣！这是御用大披风！这衣裳轻盈得就像蜘蛛网，穿在身上让人感觉仿佛赤身无物，而这正是本神布出神入化的至高精髓所在！”

paragraphs.en: So the Emperor walked along in the procession under the gorgeous canopy, and all the people in the streets and at the windows shouted: 'How incomparable are the Emperor's new clothes! what a splendid train he has to his mantle! how suitable it all is!' No one would allow that he could not see these much admired clothes; because, in doing so, he would have confessed himself a fool, or unfit for his office.
paragraphs.zh: 于是，皇帝在富丽堂皇的御盖华盖之下迈步巡游，街头巷尾以及窗台前的千千万万百姓无不齐声欢呼喝彩：“皇帝的新衣真是天下无双！披风的下摆是多么华贵庄严！浑身上下裁剪得何等合身得体啊！”谁也不愿承认自己其实什么也看不见；因为一旦承认，便等于自认是个无能的笨蛋，或者不称职的渎职者。

paragraphs.en: 'But he has got nothing on!' a little child said. 'Oh, listen to the voice of an innocent!' said the father; and one person whispered to another what the child had said. 'He has nothing on!' shouted all the people at last. The Emperor writhed, for he knew it was true. But he thought: 'The procession must go on.' So he held himself still more stiffly, and the chamberlains carried the train that was not there at all.
paragraphs.zh: “可是他身上根本什么都没穿呀！”一个小孩子天真无邪地喊出了声。“天哪，听听这无邪孩童的童言童语吧！”父亲急忙想要遮掩；然而人们开始交头接耳，将孩子的话迅速传了开来。“他当真什么都没穿！”最后全城的百姓终于异口同声爆发出了哄堂大笑与呼喊。皇帝浑身战栗，因为他心知肚明百姓说的是千真万确的真话。然而他硬着头皮暗想：“巡游大典无论如何必须坚持到底。”于是他把身子挺得更加僵直傲慢，而身后的侍从官们依然毕恭毕敬地托着那根本不存在的华丽大裙摆继续向前昂首迈进。
